kept.claim: Booking with Google Meet location and no destination calendar throws a TypeError because `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Unguarded property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` crashes Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar

**Severity:** HIGH — Booking with Google Meet location and no destination calendar throws a TypeError because `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined.

### The Problem
```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];
if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") {
```
When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`/`[]`, destructuring yields `undefined`, and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`.

### Theory / Proof
The base code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which evaluated to `undefined` and so correctly fell back to Cal Video. `handleNewBooking.ts` now sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and every other builder (`confirm.handler.ts`, webhooks, `bookingReminder.ts`) sets `[]` in that case. The `&&` only short-circuits when location is not Meet, so any Meet booking with no destination calendar reaches the dereference.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Today: bookings with a destination calendar, or with a non-Meet location, work. Breaks: a user who picks Google Meet as the location but has no destination calendar configured (exactly the case the fallback comment describes: "Google Meet is selected w/o a Google Cal"). `EventManager.create` throws, so the booking fails with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

### Research
The rest of this PR uses optional chaining for the same destructured value (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` in Google, Lark, Office365 and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`). This one site is the exception.

### Recommendation
```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];
if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar") {
  evt["location"] = "integrations:daily";
}
```
kept.evidence: EventManager.ts:118-119 destructures then dereferences `.integration` without `?.`; handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets destinationCalendar to null when no DC; MeetLocationType = integrations:google:meet (app-store/locations.ts:54); base code used `?.integration` and fell back safely.

kept.claim: Video references (Zoom, Daily, etc.) are now stored with `credentialId: undefined`, so cancelling a booking no longer deletes the video meeting.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Video booking references lose their `credentialId`

**Severity:** HIGH — Video references (Zoom, Daily, etc.) are now stored with `credentialId: undefined`, so cancelling a booking no longer deletes the video meeting.

### The Problem
```ts
credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined,
```
The base code was `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so non-calendar (video) results kept `result.credentialId`. Now every video reference is written without one.

### Theory / Proof
`createVideoEvent`/`videoClient.createMeeting` set `credentialId: credential.id` on the result (`packages/core/videoClient.ts:78`). That value is the only link from a `BookingReference` back to the video credential. `handleCancelBooking.ts:490` only deletes the meeting when the reference has one:
```ts
if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId) { ... deleteMeeting(videoCredential, uid) }
```

### What happens today vs. what will break
Today: calendar references are fine. Breaks: every new booking with a dedicated video integration (Zoom, Daily, Teams, etc.) gets a `_video` reference with `credentialId = null`. On cancellation the check above fails and `deleteMeeting` is never called, so the Zoom/Daily meeting stays around after the booking is cancelled. Any other code that resolves the video credential from the reference is affected the same way.

### Research
`updateLocation` in the same file, a few lines below (`credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`), keeps the credentialId for all result types. That is the behaviour this block should match.

### Recommendation
The calendar branch now reads `result.credentialId` too, so drop the ternary:
```ts
externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined,
credentialId: result.credentialId,
```
kept.evidence: EventManager.ts:170 drops credentialId for non-calendar results; videoClient.ts:70,78 sets credentialId on video results; handleNewBooking.ts:2121/2369 persists referencesToCreate; handleCancelBooking.ts:490 only calls deleteMeeting when video reference has credentialId; updateLocation (EventManager.ts:209) keeps result.credentialId.

kept.claim: The billing condition for `slug` was inverted: with billing enabled the org gets its slug before payment, and with billing disabled it gets neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`, so it cannot be published.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Inverted `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition in organization creation

**Severity:** HIGH — The billing condition for `slug` was inverted: with billing enabled the org gets its slug before payment, and with billing disabled it gets neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`, so it cannot be published.

### The Problem
```ts
...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),
metadata: {
  ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}),
```
The original was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The rewrite dropped the `!` on the first line, so it no longer matches the original.

### Theory / Proof
The design: when billing is off, the slug is claimed immediately. When billing is on, it is parked in `metadata.requestedSlug` and only applied after payment (`publish.handler.ts:39-58` redirects to checkout when billing is enabled, and otherwise requires `requestedSlug`). With the new code:
- billing ON: `slug` is set immediately, which skips the paid-publish step.
- billing OFF: neither is set. The org has no slug, and `publish.handler.ts:54` throws "Can't publish organization without `requestedSlug`".

### What happens today vs. what will break
Every self-hosted instance (billing off) that creates an organization ends up with one that has no slug and cannot be published. Cal.com cloud (billing on) hands out the org slug before payment. This file has nothing to do with destination calendars, so this looks like an accidental edit bundled into the PR.

### Research
`createTeams.handler.ts:67` also checks `!metadata?.requestedSlug && !organization?.slug`, which assumes exactly one of the two is set depending on billing.

### Recommendation
Revert to the original semantics (or drop the file from this PR):
```ts
...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),
metadata: {
  ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}),
```
kept.evidence: create.handler.ts:151 changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug}` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {slug} : {}`; publish.handler.ts:39-51 routes billing-on to checkout and :54-58 throws without requestedSlug when billing off, so self-hosted orgs get no slug and cannot be published.

kept.claim: Only Google selects the destination calendar by `credentialId`. Office365, Lark and CalDAV still use the first host's calendar id, so extra collective hosts on those providers get no event or a failed one.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Non-Google calendar services ignore which host/credential the event is being created for

**Severity:** HIGH — Only Google selects the destination calendar by `credentialId`. Office365, Lark and CalDAV still use the first host's calendar id, so extra collective hosts on those providers get no event or a failed one.

### The Problem
`CalendarManager.createEvent` now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` once per destination calendar. Google uses the `credentialId` to pick the matching entry. The others always take element `[0]`:
```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];
const eventsUrl = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId
  ? `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`
```
The same pattern appears in `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (`createEvent`, `createAttendees`) and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163` (CalDAV/Apple/etc.).

### Theory / Proof
For a collective event, `evt.destinationCalendar = [organizerDC, host2DC, ...]`. `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates it and calls `createEvent(host2Credential, event, host2DC.externalId)`, but the provider receives the whole array and uses `organizerDC.externalId`:
- Office365: POST `/me/calendars/<organizer's calendar id>/events` with host 2's token returns 404 (the calendar belongs to another mailbox), or lands in the wrong calendar if both use the same tenant id.
- CalDAV: `calendars.filter(c => c.externalId === organizerDC.externalId)` matches none of host 2's calendars, so no event is created and the result still looks empty/successful.
- Lark: creates in the organizer's calendar id with host 2's token and fails.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Today: works when all collective hosts use Google, or when only the first host has a calendar (the Loom demos). Breaks: the PR's stated test case, "every user with any calendar app installed should receive proper calendar events". A second host on Outlook, iCloud, CalDAV or Lark gets no event, while the reference still stores `externalCalendarId = host2DC.externalId`.

### Research
The PR already solved this for Google in `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (`destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). The `Calendar` interface now passes `credentialId` to every implementation, so the other adapters have what they need.

### Recommendation
Pick the entry by credential in each adapter, falling back to the first:
```ts
async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType> {
  const mainHostDestinationCalendar = event.destinationCalendar
    ? event.destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId) ?? event.destinationCalendar[0]
    : undefined;
```
Apply the same change in `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` and Lark. Or have `EventManager` pass a per-destination event (`{...event, destinationCalendar: [destination]}`) so adapters never see other hosts' calendars.
kept.evidence: EventManager.ts:339-371 calls createEvent per destination with the full event; only googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:145-147 selects by credentialId; office365 CalendarService.ts:73-77, lark 128-129/164-165 and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163 use element [0]; CalendarManager.ts:237-253 swallows the error while EventManager.ts:169 still records host2's externalCalendarId. Gap in the new feature, not a regression.

kept.claim: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so `?.push` silently drops every other collective host's calendar.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Team members' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none

**Severity:** MEDIUM — If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so `?.push` silently drops every other collective host's calendar.

### The Problem
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar
  ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar
  ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar]
  : null,
...
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```

### Theory / Proof
Optional-call `push` on `null` is a no-op, so `teamDestinationCalendars` is thrown away. `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` then takes the `else` branch (no destination calendar) and only creates events on the organizer's own `calendarCredentials`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Today: works if the first host (`users[0]`) has a destination calendar set. Breaks: a collective event where the first host has no destination calendar but host 2 does. Host 2 gets no calendar event, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix (#7754).

### Research
Every other builder in this PR defaults to `[]`, not `null` (`confirm.handler.ts`, `webhook.ts`, `bookingReminder.ts`), and `push` works on that.

### Recommendation
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar
  ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar
  ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar]
  : [],
...
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];
}
```
If organizer events should still go to all of the organizer's calendars when they have no destination calendar, `createAllCalendarEvents` also needs to handle a mix of "organizer without DC" and "team members with DC".
kept.evidence: handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 defaults to null; :1077-1079 `?.push` does nothing on null; EventManager.ts:338 only iterates if non-empty, else :384-396 falls back to the organizer's first calendar credential, so other hosts get no event. Gap in the new feature.

kept.claim: The new fallback `destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it never matches a real calendar. Updates on references without `externalCalendarId` now send `calendarId: undefined`.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Google update/delete fallback can never match, so the destination-calendar fallback is lost

**Severity:** MEDIUM — The new fallback `destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it never matches a real calendar. Updates on references without `externalCalendarId` now send `calendarId: undefined`.

### The Problem
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
The `find` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is `null`/`undefined`/`""`, and it compares against that same falsy value. It returns a calendar whose `externalId` is falsy, which gives a falsy `externalId`, or `undefined`. The same expression is repeated in `deleteEvent` (line 317).

### Theory / Proof
Base code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Now `updateEvent` calls `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined, ... })`. `calendarId` is a required path parameter in the Google Calendar API (`PUT /calendars/{calendarId}/events/{eventId}`), so the call is rejected. `deleteEvent` falls back to `"primary"` instead of the destination calendar. That 404s for events in a secondary calendar, and the 404 is swallowed as success (`if (err.code === 404) return resolve()`), so the event is silently left in place.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Today: bookings whose reference has `externalCalendarId` (created after that field was introduced) are fine. Breaks: older bookings/references with a null `externalCalendarId` (e.g. `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` passes `calenderExternalId = null` when the reference has none) can no longer be rescheduled or cancelled in Google when they were in a non-primary destination calendar.

### Research
`createEvent` in this same file uses the correct approach, matching by `credentialId`.

### Recommendation
Fall back to the first (main host) destination calendar as before:
```ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId || "primary";
```
Apply the same in `deleteEvent`.
kept.evidence: googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:254-256 and :315-317 run `find` only when externalCalendarId is falsy; schema.prisma:153 externalId is non-null String so it never matches; EventManager.ts:505-508 passes null for references without externalCalendarId; update then sends calendarId undefined (required path param); delete falls back to 'primary' and a 404 resolves silently. Regression vs base `destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

kept.claim: The recurring-cancel block now runs once per calendar reference but always deletes only the organizer's first reference of each booking, so it deletes the same events N times and never deletes the other hosts' recurring events.
kept.evidence: handleCancelBooking.ts:418-484: the recurring branch inside the per-reference loop ignores `reference`, iterates organizer credentials only and uses `updBooking.references.find(...)` (first ref only). Collective bookings now have K references, so hosts 2..K keep their recurring occurrences. The repeated deletes are harmless (Google resolves 404/410, CalendarService.ts:333-335).

kept.claim: The credential-from-DB fallback is duplicated in `createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateAllCalendarEvents`, and in `createAllCalendarEvents` each host's DB lookup and provider `createEvent` call are awaited one after another, so collective booking creation latency grows linearly with host count.
kept.evidence: EventManager.ts:337-383 and 503-551 duplicate the credential DB fallback. In createAllCalendarEvents both the DB lookup and createEvent are awaited sequentially per host. In updateAllCalendarEvents only the DB lookup is sequential; updateEvent promises are pushed un-awaited and run concurrently. Impact is modest for typical host counts.

dropped.claim: The new `loadUsers` try/catch turns all non-Prisma errors, including its own input-validation error, into HTTP 500 "Unable to load users", and turns Prisma DB errors into 400.
dropped.evidence: Not new behaviour: getServerErrorFromUnknown.ts:45-47 already maps PrismaClientKnownRequestError to 400; before the PR, an empty dynamicUserList led to ensureAvailableUsers throwing a plain Error (handleNewBooking.ts:429), which getServerErrorFromUnknown.ts:64-65 maps to 500. Only the message text changed.
